mission: Ben and Talon confirm the offworld destination and finalize the off-grid transit plan. Luke can only offer limited quiet support without making the case official. They prepare to leave.
why_now: Everything that can be confirmed has been confirmed. Everything that could be destroyed has been destroyed. The Vigil is already moving on Iresh and the only move left is to go. This is the last moment in the apartment before the act turns.
conflict: The logistics of the off-grid transit are real and specific — civilian cargo hauler, no Jedi credentials, no official backing. Luke can offer limited quiet support without making the case official, but 'quiet support' means very little if something goes wrong on Iresh. Ben is going in without a net and knows it.
turning_point: Act turn. Ben and Talon leave for Iresh, knowing the Vigil/Foundation is already moving to recover something Jacen left there.
closing_hook: Act turn. Ben and Talon leave for Iresh, knowing the Vigil/Foundation is already moving to recover something Jacen left there.
setting: Coruscant, the Skywalker family apartment then a low-profile civilian transit dock. Ben and Talon finalize the off-grid transit plan, pack what little gear they can carry, and board a civilian cargo hauler bound for Iresh. Luke offers what quiet support he can from Shedu Maad without making the case official.

stakes.personal: Ben is going to Iresh to use Jacen’s crisis logic against Jacen’s surviving student, in service of stopping Jacen’s unfinished work from being weaponized. The self-definition engine is running: he’s not going because Luke told him to or because the Order validated it. He’s going because he decided. That’s a different kind of weight.
stakes.interpersonal: Talon doesn’t make a speech about this. He packs his bag and complains about the hauler’s cargo-class passenger compartment. The decision is already made; the tone is professional. The friendship that’s been forming through action is simply present — two people preparing for the same dangerous thing without needing to name what they are to each other.
stakes.external: The Vigil/Foundation expedition is already on Iresh under legitimate cover. The off-grid transit plan means no backup, no official status, and no legal protection if it goes wrong. Luke is doing what he can from where he is. That’s less than either of them wishes it were.

sensory_details: The apartment in the early hours: the same recycled air and low light, Talon's chair still facing the door. The packs they're taking are small — civilian-cover small, nothing that announces them. The transit dock is a low-traffic civilian freight slip, the kind that smells of fuel cell residue and has queuing droids that never quite stop moving. The cargo hauler's interior is functional and anonymous.

turning_point_detail.trigger: Ben and Talon board the civilian cargo hauler. The dock logistics are complete. There is nothing left to confirm or prepare.
turning_point_detail.shift: The Act Two investigation closes and Act Three expedition begins. Ben and Talon leave Coruscant for Iresh, knowing the Vigil/Foundation is already there recovering something Jacen left behind.
turning_point_detail.cost: They are going off-grid, without official status, without the documentary case Ben was building, with a framed conviction on Talon's record and a prison-break on Ben's. If they are wrong, they answer for it without institutional backing. If they are right, the evidence will have to be the operation itself.

emotional_arc.start: Ben is composed and operational — practical logistics, quiet preparation. The decision was made chapters ago; this scene executes it.
emotional_arc.shift: The moment of boarding: the apartment left behind, the family holo on the shelf for the second time, the transit dock's anonymous industrial air. The weight is real but not melodramatic.
emotional_arc.end: They are on the hauler. Iresh is the destination. The story has moved from investigation to expedition. Ben feels the shift as something close to relief — the ambiguity of what to do is over.

key_beats.beat_description: Final preparations in the apartment: small packs, civilian cover, nothing that announces them; Talon claims the better bunk allocation through sustained complaint.
key_beats.state_change: The decision made chapters ago executes as logistics — the emotional weight of leaving is carried by what the room has held, not by what is said.
key_beats.pov_reaction: The family holo on the shelf noted and left — not approached, not named — and the particular act of choosing not to say goodbye to a room.

key_beats.beat_description: Luke's quiet support is confirmed — limited, off-record, from Shedu Maad; both of them understand what 'limited' means without it being said.
key_beats.state_change: The safety net is real and genuinely insufficient — Luke is doing what he can, and what he can do is very little if something goes wrong on Iresh.
key_beats.pov_reaction: The acknowledgment arriving without relief — limited understood not as criticism of Luke but as the actual shape of what exists.

key_beats.beat_description: Ben and Talon transit to the low-profile civilian freight dock: queuing droids, fuel-cell smell, anonymous infrastructure that doesn't ask questions.
key_beats.state_change: Coruscant is behind them — operationally, legally, as a place to return to if this goes wrong.
key_beats.pov_reaction: The transit happening in the register of task completion — not anticipation, the execution of a decision already fully made.

key_beats.beat_description: Ben and Talon board the civilian cargo hauler; the dock logistics complete; there is nothing left to confirm or prepare.
key_beats.state_change: The Act Two investigation closes — the last door that could have stopped this is now behind them.
key_beats.pov_reaction: Something close to relief arriving as the hauler seals — the ambiguity of what to do replaced by the clarity of being in motion.

key_beats.beat_description: The hauler departs for Iresh; the Vigil/Foundation expedition is already there under legitimate cover; Ben and Talon are going off-grid with no backup and no official status.
key_beats.state_change: The story shifts from investigation to expedition — the evidence from here will have to be the operation itself.
key_beats.pov_reaction: The shift registered as something that has already happened — not a new feeling, the recognition of a change that was made a long time ago.
